findings.reason: §4's spec must name the module→distribution map (an extended owner interface, e.g. exposed from `build_census`/`module_distribution_map`) in its scratch hand-off, otherwise its stated acceptance rule is unimplementable without duplicating `module_distribution_map()`, which is exactly the fork the scratch channel exists to prevent.
findings.text: §4 says it writes "its optional set" to the run's scratch and reads it in the fresh environment, but its acceptance rule is that an optional module "fails with ModuleNotFoundError naming a distribution the census classed optional"; that decision needs the census's module→distribution mapping, which `module_distribution_map()` builds from the shared environment's installed distributions via `importlib.metadata.packages_distributions()` — the very distributions that are absent in the fresh environment the walk runs in, so the mapping cannot be rebuilt there and the driver must either fork it or the scratch interface must carry it. Nothing in the `Census` dataclass (rows keyed by distribution, with no module→distribution field) carries it either.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new repository module is proposed (the §4 driver is deliberately a run artifact), and the one substantial module the plan did add, `tests/test_declared_dependencies.py`, hides the import walk, distribution mapping and transitive closure behind the single `build_census()` entry point rather than spreading them across shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4's scratch interface carries only the census's optional distribution set, but its acceptance rule needs the module→distribution mapping owned by `tests/test_declared_dependencies.py` (`module_distribution_map`).
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §4 states it adds no public surface (the driver is a run artifact, the fragment is the only file it adds) and §5 adds only per-test pytest marks, so no section adds to any of the four families and none is required to name a retirement or merge.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the machinery it extends (`tests/test_declared_dependencies.py` for `OPTIONAL_SUBSYSTEM_ROOTS` and the census; `imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.py:149` `staging_cache_root()` for the node-local `TMPDIR` convention), and a search of the tree (`.github/workflows/` absent, no `Makefile`/`taskfile`, no `scripts/` env builder, no existing module-import walker) finds no fresh-environment or import-walk machinery the plan is rebuilding.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — nothing is wrapped. §4 consumes the census owner through a documented scratch hand-off rather than layering over it, and §5 uses pytest-timeout's own per-test `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)` mark rather than a parallel mechanism.
